## Summary

Adds the JiuwenSwarm startup-latency work as **one consolidated patch** (`0010-jw-startup-latency.patch`, ~35s of per-launch savings). The changes were developed and measured on the Windows desktop line (same-machine A/B against gateway startup stage logs):

| change | measured saving |
|---|---|
| feishu SDK lazy import (it was imported even with the channel disabled) | ~4.7s |
| `tui_connect` preload off the critical path | ~1.8s |
| channel-config settle window 0.75s -> 0.2s | ~0.55s |
| heartbeat import chain deferred | ~2.8s |
| AgentServer import slimming (pandas/pdfplumber/milvus out of the import path) | ~6.8s |
| Gateway<->AgentServer connect unblocked from warmup | ~9.5s |
| post-listen warmups gated behind the first request | ~15.6s |

End-to-end on the Windows desktop: warm restart ~17.5s -> ~5-7s; user-perceived cold start 50s+ -> 20-25s.

**Why one patch instead of seven**: the changes overlap on `app_gateway.py` / `agent_ws_server.py`, and a chain where several patches edit the same region cannot pass the idempotent-reapply contract (`swarm-patches.py apply` twice must be a no-op — the `--reverse --check` skip needs each patch's post-state intact). Consolidating keeps one patch per file region, matching the upstream patch-set convention.

## Test plan

- [x] `swarm-patches.py apply` on a clean `workswarm0.2.6` checkout with 0001-0009 + this patch — passes
- [x] **second `apply` over the already-patched tree — no-op (the previously failing idempotency case)**
- [x] `swarm-patches.py verify` — passes
- [ ] CI green

707.author: HugoXK
707.body:
Fixes #706.

`CasStore.read()` walked three candidate paths but re-threw on the first copy that failed its SHA-256 re-hash, so an intact copy in the next layout was never read (`packages/cas/src/index.ts:94-105` against `:148-153`). A corrupt copy in the current pool therefore reported a recoverable object as lost, and the API endpoint turned it into a 404 `CAS blob missing for this content_hash`.

### Change

- `read()` decides on the file read alone: only `ENOENT` falls through to the next layout, the digest check sits outside the `try`, and total loss raises a typed `CasIntegrityError` instead of a message literal. `verify()` tests that type, so rewording a message can no longer change which copy wins.
- The web-page content route (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:2967-2976`) reads the blob once and maps `ENOENT` to the existing 404, instead of asking `has()` first. Corruption therefore stays the route's loud `500` + `apiLog.warn("web_page_content_failed")` even after #680 makes `has()` answer `false` instead of throwing — the pair would otherwise have collapsed corruption into "never stored", the outcome #706 criterion 2 forbids.
- `stream()` and `retain()` are unchanged in this PR (same first-path-wins shape; #708 tracks them rather than widening this diff).

### Tests

`packages/cas/src/index.test.ts`:

1. corrupt pool copy + intact legacy `cas/sha256/<first-two>/<hash>` copy → `read()` returns the original bytes, and `has()`/`verify()` both answer `true` for that same layout (pins the contract a later `has()` cleanup could silently undo).
2. the other pool's layout (`versioning/data/...`) as the only intact copy → `read()` returns it.
3. a non-`ENOENT` filesystem failure (`EISDIR`) is not reported as corruption.
4. every candidate corrupt → `read()` rejects with `CAS integrity failure`; a hash that was never stored keeps `CAS object not found` with `code: "ENOENT"`.

`services/api/src/server.test.ts` (WPC-002): after the existing missing-blob 404, the same blob is rewritten with corrupt bytes and the route must answer `500 WebPage content read failed`, not the 404 — the guard for the #680 composition.

### Run on this tip

CAS suite, `tsx --test` over `packages/cas/src/index.test.ts` against the package source, run in the tree:

```
# index.ts from base 3fe9f9c9, this PR's test file:
not ok 4 - a corrupt pool copy falls back to the intact legacy layout
not ok 5 - the other pool's layout is a fallback candidate too
# tests 8 / # pass 6 / # fail 2

# index.ts at this tip:
# tests 8 / # pass 8 / # fail 0
```

Not run locally: `services/api/src/server.test.ts` (the route guard above). That assertion is verified by the UT job on this tip, not by a local run of that file, and the base 3fe9f9c9 numbers above come from the CAS file only.

Owner: ScienceDiscovery Dev-2
Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Dev-Lead

709.author: HugoXK
709.body:
Fixes #708

## Contract change: a corrupt pool copy no longer fails materialization

`services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.test.ts:63-66` was written before `#707`: it corrupts one copy and requires the whole request to fail. With `stream()` now verifying each candidate and falling through to an intact one, that expectation is stale — the request succeeds **and publishes the whole object**, never the corrupt bytes.

This PR changes that expectation, and nothing about the accessor's logic: **`packages/cas/src/index.ts` is untouched in this push.** The only `packages/cas` change is one added test case; the production change in `stream()`/`retain()` shipped in the previous push of this branch.

Why the two halves of `#708` are pinned in two different layers:

- **API level** (`services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.test.ts`): only `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/<hash>` is overwritten, so the request falls back to the intact mirror in `versioning/data` and must succeed with `served.sha256` equal to the original hash and the destination bytes equal to the original object.
- **CAS level** (`packages/cas/src/index.test.ts`, probe (a), already on this branch): both typed pools absent, an intact copy only in the legacy `cas/sha256/<xx>/<hash>` layout — `stream()` must yield exactly the original bytes and no error. That is the legacy-only case the API test cannot reach, because a workspace publication on a store whose `versioning/data` copy is corrupt hits the lease snapshot scan first and reports `Object integrity failure` (`PUBLICATION_UNCONFIRMED`) — a different exit, from the scanner rather than from `stream()`. Recorded as a follow-up candidate, not fixed here.

With every copy corrupt, the API test still requires an integrity-shaped rejection (`/integrity|checksum|size/i`, matched across the error and its cause) and no destination file, so "never publish a partial destination" keeps its guard.

## Measurements

Every pair below is **the same test file, the same command, in the same checkout** — the only thing that changes between the two runs of a pair is `packages/cas/src/index.ts` (`0e7075c4`'s version versus this tip's version). It is one test sample run twice, not two test samples.

```
node --import tsx --test packages/cas/src/index.test.ts

  index.ts = main 0e7075c4   -> # tests 12 / # pass 9  / # fail 3
                                 not ok 9  stream() does not hand out a corrupt pool copy when the legacy copy is intact
                                 not ok 10 stream() emits no bytes when every copy is corrupt
                                 not ok 11 retain() promotes the intact legacy copy instead of giving up on the corrupted pool copy
  index.ts = this tip       -> # tests 12 / # pass 12 / # fail 0
```

```
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "immutable artifact edit" services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.test.ts

  index.ts = main 0e7075c4   -> # tests 2 / # pass 0 / # fail 2
                                 not ok 1 - immutable artifact edit roundtrip, binary=false
                                   error: 'CAS integrity failure'
                                 not ok 2 - immutable artifact edit roundtrip, binary=true
                                   error: 'CAS integrity failure'
  index.ts = this tip       -> # tests 2 / # pass 2 / # fail 0
```

The new twelfth case (`stream() leaves an intact first layout untouched across several chunks`, 400KB, asserts more than one chunk and the exact byte sequence) passes in both directions by design: it is the "unchanged behaviour" probe of `#708`, not a fix.

## Scope

- `packages/cas/src/index.ts` — unchanged in this push.
- `packages/cas/src/index.test.ts` — one added case (probe (c)); probes (a) and (b) and the `retain()` case are the ones already on this branch, not new behaviour introduced here.
- `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.test.ts` — the stale contract, rewritten as described above.

## Checks

- `Base: 0e7075c475fe657a7e772d7efdaa55cab1bcd9ba`
- Branch: `dev2/fix/cas-stream-retain-fallback`
- Both pairs above were executed with `node --import tsx --test` inside an isolated workspace install of this tree; the pre-existing `pnpm --recursive typecheck` failure on `main` itself (missing `node_modules` for `packages/execution-router`) is unchanged by this PR and is why the run above is the file-level one.

711.author: HugoXK
711.body:
Fixes #710

## Base

- `Base: 0e7075c475fe657a7e772d7efdaa55cab1bcd9ba` (live `main`, 2026-11-01T17:05:39Z)
- Branch: `dev1/fix/run-stream-turn-placement`
- Five commits: three that add only tests, two that change `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/`.

| Commit | What | Diff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `38cef9bd28b2ba1f9b08d199357a44c470f98549` | the reported reproduction, test only | 1 file, +14/−0 |
| `988bad60` | second shape: text waits even when a tool event already opened its turn, test only | 1 file, +23/−0 |
| `4d8d8bab` | the fix | 2 files, +106/−23 |
| `d3e585e7` | replay-level guard: text whose turn was never named is not dropped, test only | 1 file, +13/−0 |
| `6833ebb4` | keep “a block is pending or placed, never both” true on every path | 1 file, +8/−2 |

## Red first

Both reproducing tests were measured alone on top of `main`'s reducer, so the numbers below are the failure, not a paraphrase of it.

With only the reported test (`38cef9bd`, on `main` `0e7075c4`):

```
$ cd apps/desktop && node --import tsx --test tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts
# tests 39
# pass 38
# fail 1
```

```
not ok 9 - a later turn's text is not folded into turn 1 when its response.started arrives late
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
        'first turn',
    +   'HELLO WORLD'
      ]
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
```

With both reproducing tests (`988bad60`, still `main`'s reducer):

```
# tests 40
# pass 38
# fail 2
```

```
not ok 10 - text for an unknown response waits for its turn even after a tool event opened that turn
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
        [
          'first turn'
        ],
    +   [
    +     'HELLO'
    +   ]
    -   []
      ]
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
```

The second failure is the important one: it fails because the text was **placed at all** before its turn was known — not because it landed on the wrong turn number. A patch that only rewrites the hard-coded `turn: 1` leaves it passing the first test and failing this one.

`d3e585e7` is a guard rather than a reproduction: it is green on `0e7075c4` too (the old reducer placed such text immediately), and it pins that the new buffer never drops text a stream failed to name.

## Why it happens (read on `0e7075c4`)

- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:404-411` — `locateTurn` returns the first turn that owns the `responseId`, and when no turn owns it, falls back to `state.turns.at(-1)`. That fallback is what put a later turn's text under the turn before it.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:366-382` — because of that fallback, `withResponse`'s “no turn at all” branch only runs when `turns` is empty, so it is not the source of the misfiling even though it hard-codes `turn: 1`.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:107-111` — `assistant.response.started` added a blank block to its own turn and never looked for the block the earlier frame had created, so the same response existed twice: the text in the previous turn, an empty block in its own turn.
- `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts:139-142` — the existing coverage is a single-turn orphan with no `responseId` and no second turn, which is why this gap was green.

## The fix

- `RunStreamState.pendingResponses` (`apps/desktop/src/run-stream/model.ts`) holds text that arrived before the frame naming its turn, keyed by `responseId`. Until `assistant.response.started` arrives, no turn is known, so nothing is placed and nothing can be misfiled.
- `withStartedResponse` places the buffered block whole — text, truncation and settlement — on the turn the frame names, and drops any buffered copy for the same id so a block is pending or placed, never both. A redelivered start frame is a no-op.
- `flushPendingResponses` runs on `closeRunStream` and on `run.completed`: a stream that never names the response still shows its text, on the newest turn (turn 1 when nothing else arrived) — the old placement, used only as the last resort it should have been.
- `turnOwning` resolves a `responseId` to the **newest** turn that owns it, so a duplicate can never pin every later delta back to an earlier turn.
- The `responseId === undefined` path for older records is untouched: an unidentified frame still routes to the newest response of the newest turn, and still opens a block there when there is none. The doc comment above `withResponse` was rewritten to describe what the code now does, including the buffer.

### One trade-off, stated rather than hidden

`hasVisibleAnswer` (`apps/desktop/src/run-stream/model.ts:181-184`) reads `turns` and `finalContent`, so a buffered block contributes nothing while the stream is still open: in the case this PR is about — an unreadable `assistant.response.started` with the deltas intact — the answer appears when the run ends instead of immediately in the wrong turn. Replay is unaffected because `foldRunRecords` calls `closeRunStream` first (`apps/desktop/src/run-stream/replay.ts:54-62`), and the live transcript view does not consult `hasVisibleAnswer`.

## Ran / Not run

- Ran: `cd apps/desktop && node --import tsx --test tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts` → `# tests 40 / # pass 40 / # fail 0` (was `40 / 38 / 2` on `main`).
- Ran: `node --import tsx --test tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts tests/replay.test.ts` → `# tests 56 / # pass 56 / # fail 0`.
- Ran: `cd apps/desktop && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → `# tests 683 / # suites 93 / # pass 683 / # fail 0`.
- Ran: `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit` → exit 0.
- Ran: an include-the-test-files probe (`apps/desktop`'s own config excludes `**/*.test.ts`, so `tsc -p apps/desktop` never sees them) → no error in any file this PR touches; the errors it reports are in `apps/desktop/tests/tool-io.test.ts`, `assistant-turn.test.tsx`, `conversation.test.tsx`, `language.test.tsx`, `model-form-combo.test.tsx`, `remote-format.test.ts`, `api-permissions.test.ts` and two CSS side-effect imports, none of them changed here.
- Not run: `pnpm --recursive typecheck` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` both fail **before** this branch, on `main` `0e7075c4` itself, with identical output: `packages/execution-router` has no `node_modules` in this checkout (`[ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL] … Cannot find module '@sciencediscovery/schema'`, and pnpm reports `Local package.json exists, but node_modules missing`), plus 7 pre-existing errors in `services/api` and `packages/execution-router`. `pnpm install` cannot repair it here because the store is read-only. The root test config does not include `apps/*/tests`, so neither command covers this PR's test files anyway.

## Scope

Four files, all under `apps/desktop/`: `src/run-stream/model.ts`, `src/run-stream/reducer.ts`, `tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts`, `tests/replay.test.ts`.

## Trade-off recorded (second reviewer Low, deliberately not changed)

Text buffered on `pendingResponses` contributes nothing to `hasVisibleAnswer` (`apps/desktop/src/run-stream/model.ts:181-184`) until the frame that names its turn arrives, so in a **live** view the answer appears when the run completes — `run.completed` and `closeRunStream` flush the buffer — rather than as the deltas arrive. Replay is unaffected: it flushes through `closeRunStream` before rendering, which `tests/replay.test.ts` now pins ("a replay whose start frame was lost still shows the text that buffered"). That delay is the intended cost of "delayed, never dropped": placing the text immediately is exactly what put a later turn's answer under the turn before it.

Benched, not in this PR: nothing from the review is outstanding — the stale-buffer path was fixed structurally in `6833ebb4` (`pending XOR placed` by construction) and the replay coverage case landed in the same commit.

714.author: HugoXK
714.body:
Fixes #713

`readMultipartUploads` reads `Content-Disposition` with a single regex, `/\bfilename\*?=(?:UTF-8''|")?([^";]+)"?/i`, so a quoted value ends at its first `;`; every captured name is then percent-decoded, including the plain `filename` parameter that browsers send verbatim (RFC 7578 §4.2). This PR replaces that with a quote-aware parameter scan: a quoted value runs to its closing quote (backslash-escaped quotes included), a plain `filename` is used exactly as sent, and only `filename*` is percent-decoded, once. The decoded name still goes through `sanitizeUploadFilename`, so the basename guard is unchanged.

It also carries both findings from the review at `68c8d5b0`:

- **Unusable `filename*` falls back to `filename`** (RFC 6266 §4.3). `decodeExtendedFilename` now reports "no usable name" when the value is empty, decodes to nothing, or is not percent-decodable, and the parser uses the plain parameter instead of letting the broken extended value win.
- **An unusable name fails only its own entry** (#713's third expectation). `uploadWorkspaceParts` records `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` against that entry through the existing per-entry `failed` channel instead of aborting the batch, so the valid files in the same request still land. A request whose every entry is rejected for its name still throws, so WSP-003 keeps its 400-and-nothing-written answer for a lone traversal upload (`services/api/src/server.test.ts` WSP-003 is unchanged and green).

Scope note, not changed here: part headers are still read as one line, so a folded `Content-Disposition` header keeps its existing truncation.

Tip SHA: 90b0567701263a4f38f98a9d943f821b225442b4

715.author: ink999107
715.body:
## Problem

An evolve proposal defaults to `thinking: "disabled"`, and the per-call ceiling follows that setting: 16k for PUCT. On a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway the `thinking` field is accepted and ignored — the model reasons anyway, so every mutation came back at exactly 16k output tokens with no content at all. The sidecar reports each one as "the model spent all 16000 output tokens on hidden thinking", and the run spends its whole budget producing candidates that are recorded as ones that would not run.

## Fix

- `endpointCanDisableThinking(model)` answers whether the endpoint can actually be told to stop thinking: the wire variant has to map the toggle (`THINKING_CONTROL_VARIANTS`), and the catalog or the operator's own `thinkingSupported` fact can override it.
- `assembleGoal` records `thinking: "enabled"` when the requested "disabled" cannot be honored, so the ceiling follows the thinking floor (96k for PUCT) rather than the quiet one.
- Pre-flight applies the same rule for a goal that arrives any other way, and its refusal no longer offers "turn thinking off" as a way out of a ceiling that this endpoint would ignore.

## The budget the user is asked to approve

Recording the change is not enough: the checkpoint that asks the user to spend only carried the run's shape, and the numbers that decide whether the search can finish arrived afterwards.

- `get_evolve_budget` returns what `create_evolve_run` will apply — the thinking setting the run will record (with a note when the request cannot be honored), the per-call ceiling for each algorithm, and the run's total token and wall-clock caps.
- The `evolve-design` skill requires reading it at Checkpoint 3 and stating the ceiling times the expansion count against the total, instead of promising a setting the run will not have.
- `MIN_TOKENS_PER_CALL` is shared between the proposal path and pre-flight. They disagreed: the path wrote 96k for every algorithm while pre-flight demanded 128k for OpenEvolve, so choosing thinking on an OpenEvolve run was refused by the default the path had just written for it.

## Evidence

A realistic mutation prompt (the codec task from the failing run, 1,839 prompt tokens) against the same gateway at a 96k ceiling: 26,963 reasoning tokens before the first content token, 28,416 completion tokens in total, and a complete reply in 181 s. The 16k ceiling could never have reached the content.

A full PUCT run on that gateway after the change: `thinking=enabled`, `ceiling=96000`, 17 model calls, **0 calls with no content**, 586,941 tokens, and the gate score moved from 0.283 to 0.721 (test split 0.717).

## Tests

- `node --import tsx --test src/evolution/model-thinking.test.ts src/evolution/preflight.test.ts src/evolution/proposal.test.ts src/evolution/call-budget.test.ts` — 48/48.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/evolve test` — 11/11.


Closes #780

722.body:
Fixes #721

Owner: Dev2
Written-by: Dev-2
Base: 8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f
Tip SHA: 53b643e2d56dc2fa5b685ad91fc2b11756e8475d

A finished run reported `bestTestScore` — one evaluation of one candidate — as evidence that the search improved something it never optimised against. That number cannot support the claim: 5/8 against a 5/8 baseline and 8/8 against 3/8 print the same "improvement". This pairs the winner with the run's own starting program on the same held-out cases and reports an exact two-sided sign test next to the point estimate.

## What changed

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/acceptance.py` (new): `paired_evidence(baseline, candidate, alpha=0.05)` → `{wins, losses, ties, n, pValue, alpha, verdict}`. Exact paired sign test via `math.comb` (no normal approximation, no invented ranks); ties drop out, cases only one side ran are not counted. `established` needs both `pValue <= alpha` **and** `wins > losses`; the p-value is two-sided, so a significant result in the other direction is `not established` and the direction stays readable from `wins`/`losses`/`pValue`. `insufficient` covers fewer than six decided cases and balanced splits.
- `test_gate_domain.py`: `caseResults` carries the existing `selected` map (case id → passed) out of the domain, so the pairing survives the rate.
- `puct_engine.finish()`: evaluates the tree's root program on the same held-out shards as the winner, pairs by case id, and emits `gate_evidence`. When there are no test shards, no per-case results, or the baseline evaluation raises, it leaves the field **absent** and says why in the run log — it is never zero-filled, because "no evidence" and "evidence of no improvement" send the reader to different places.
- `events.search_finished()` + `packages/schema/src/evolution.ts` `SearchFinished`: optional `gateEvidence` / `gate_evidence`, so existing readers keep working unchanged.

## Red first

Command (host interpreter, `src` on the path — see "Not run" for why not `uv`):

```
$ cd services/evolve && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest tests/test_acceptance.py -q
```

Output before the fix (the probe from the issue):

```
    def test_search_finished_reports_paired_gate_evidence() -> None:
        event = events.search_finished("completed", 3, 12, best_test_score=0.625,
                                       stop_reason="budget", expansions_planned=20)
>       assert "gateEvidence" in event, sorted(event)
E       AssertionError: ['bestNodeIndex', 'bestTestScore', 'candidates', 'expansionsPlanned', 'status', 'stopReason', ...]
E       assert 'gateEvidence' in {'bestNodeIndex': 3, 'bestTestScore': 0.625, 'candidates': 12, 'expansionsPlanned': 20, ...}
1 failed
```

On the tip above, the same command reports `16 passed`.

The probe is kept under its issue name and now passes the paired result into the new argument; the field stays optional on purpose, and `test_a_finish_event_with_no_evidence_carries_no_field` pins the absent case (the serializer has no evidence to invent).

## Review follow-up on this branch

Two correctness findings from review, fixed in the two commits under the tip:

- **`established` requires a positive direction.** The p-value is two-sided, so 0 wins / 6 losses (p = 0.03125) used to be reported as `established`: the strongest possible regression read as the strongest possible improvement. The rule is now `pValue <= alpha and wins > losses`, and the opposite direction is `not established`. Pinned by `test_a_significant_regression_is_never_established` (0-6 and 0-8); the existing 8-0 `established`, 7-1 `not established` and 3-3 `insufficient` assertions are unchanged.
- **A raising baseline evaluation no longer fails a finished run.** When the gate raises instead of returning invalid for the starting program (no JUnit report, a failed setup, unparsable XML), `finish()` catches it, logs `warn` with `str(error)[:300]`, and keeps `gateEvidence` absent. Before, the exception escaped to `server.py`, which would replace a completed search with `search_finished("failed", None, 0)`. Only the baseline evaluation is guarded; the winner's evaluation keeps its existing behaviour. Pinned by `test_a_baseline_evaluation_that_raises_does_not_fail_the_finished_run` (status stays not-failed, `bestTestScore` still 0.625, field absent, log says why).

Red before the two fixes, then green:

```
$ cd services/evolve && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest tests/test_acceptance.py -q
3 failed, 13 passed

$ cd services/evolve && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest tests/test_acceptance.py -q
16 passed
```

The two new assertions at the tip:

```
tests/test_acceptance.py::test_a_significant_regression_is_never_established[6] PASSED
tests/test_acceptance.py::test_a_significant_regression_is_never_established[8] PASSED
tests/test_acceptance.py::test_a_baseline_evaluation_that_raises_does_not_fail_the_finished_run PASSED
3 passed
```

## Gates

Acceptance command from the issue (`tests/test_acceptance.py tests/test_puct_engine.py`), same pytest, host interpreter:

```
$ cd services/evolve && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest tests/test_acceptance.py tests/test_puct_engine.py -q
73 passed
```

Targeted neighbours added by this change:

```
$ cd services/evolve && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest tests/test_acceptance.py tests/test_puct_engine.py tests/test_test_gate.py -q
84 passed
```

The statistic itself, at the boundaries: 8-0 → `established` (p = 0.0078125), 6-0 → `established` (p = 0.03125), 7-1 → `not established` (p = 0.0703125), 3-3 → `insufficient`, empty → `insufficient`, 0-6 (p = 0.03125) and 0-8 (p = 0.0078125) → `not established` (significant regression, not improvement), 5/8 vs 3/8 at the engine level (positive point estimate 0.625) → `not established`.

Full evolve suite (360 passed, 8 failed) — the 8 failures reproduce identically on a clean worktree of base `8bcc2237`, so they are this box's environment, not this change:

```
$ git worktree add --detach base 8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f
$ cd base/services/evolve && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest tests/test_idea_tree.py tests/test_measurement.py tests/test_puct_end_to_end.py tests/test_puct_fidelity.py -q
8 failed, 28 passed
```

Reasons: `test_idea_tree` needs Python ≥3.12 (`fromisoformat` rejects the `Z` suffix on this host's 3.10) and the other three need the `candidates` runtime (`No module named 'pandas'`) — `services/evolve` requires Python ≥3.12. CI runs 3.12 in the project venv.

Schema package (type changed):

```
$ cd packages/schema && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json          # exit 0
$ cd packages/schema && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit # exit 0
$ cd packages/schema && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"           # 29 passed
$ cd apps/web && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit        # exit 0
```

## Not run

- `uv run --extra test pytest ...`: `uv sync` needs network for this box's cache (`scipy==1.18.0` / `uvloop==0.22.1` absent offline), so the commands above use the host interpreter with `PYTHONPATH=src`. CI runs the issue's exact `uv run` command.
- Repo-level UT/L2 and Docker/binary layers: no `/ci-cache`, needs networked `uv` — left to CI.

## Caveat kept from the issue

The exact sign test assumes the paired gate cases are independent. Cases from one suite can correlate (shared fixtures, one broken import, one flaky test), which makes the p-value optimistic. The verdict is evidence at a stated alpha, never a guarantee; a later change may replace the statistic with a cluster-aware one if suites show correlation.

```
$ cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/MemoryGraphEscapeGuard.test.tsx
# /home/xuke/work/sciencediscovery-dev-1/apps/web/tests/MemoryGraphEscapeGuard.test.tsx:21

The two wiring assertions describe the state of `main` directly: `git show 8bcc2237:apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx | grep 'event.key === "Escape"'` → `1052: const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent) => { if (event.key === "Escape") onClose(); };`, and `git show 8bcc2237:apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx | grep -c onNestedWindowChange` → `0`.

- `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1051-1055` — the explorer's window-level Escape called `onClose()` unconditionally.
- `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:719-726` — the artifact modal guards the same key on `!csvWindowOpen && !molstarOpen`, but returns early when `embedded`, which is exactly how the explorer renders it (`MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1700-1715`). In that state the explorer's handler was the only one left.
- `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/CsvArtifactWindow.tsx:156-168` and `apps/web/src/MolstarWindow.tsx:129-133` both bind Escape and neither stops propagation, so one keypress ran the nested window's handler and the explorer's.
- `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphTour.tsx:74-87` already guards this collision for the tour (capture phase + `stopPropagation`, comment: "not the whole explorer"); the embedded artifact windows never got the equivalent.

- `shouldCloseOnEscape(csvWindowOpen, molstarOpen)` is exported from `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx`, next to the existing `shouldFocusEntryNode` predicate, and returns `!csvWindowOpen && !molstarOpen`.

- The panel also reports "nothing open" when it unmounts: it can go away with a CSV/Mol* window still open (the user selects a node without an artifact), and without that reset the explorer would keep believing a layer was stacked above it and its Escape would stop working.
- Standalone behavior is untouched: `onNestedWindowChange` is optional, no caller passes it outside the explorer, and the `embedded` early return in the existing guard is unchanged.

Net observable: with a CSV workspace or Mol* viewer open inside the explorer, one Escape closes that window and the explorer stays mounted with its selection, filters, unfolded set and viewport; the next Escape closes the explorer.

No rendered markup, class or stylesheet changed — the visible states of the explorer and of both windows are the same, so there is no visual surface to inspect beyond these windows.

A live run folds adjacent exploration steps into a collapsed `<details class="timeline-exploration">` (`apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx`). It retains transport, enabled state, URL, commands/arguments, environment, headers, timeouts, credentials, OAuth and discovered tools. Saving performs no catalog discovery, connection, STDIO process or OAuth flow.

MCP configuration is an external encrypted-file authority, so this also completes the required external-control commit path: freeze approval/CAS, journal submission intent, submit once outside SQLite, then recover only through an authoritative operation receipt. Unknown/late responses never trigger resubmission or an invented success/failure. A negative resolution writes a tombstone that fences delayed submits. Stop before dispatch suppresses the write; Stop after a committed write records the saved fact while suppressing activation/continuation. Failed SQLite receipt storage can recover the exact authority receipt without reapplying. Unattached backends expose existing cards read-only.

The authority atomically renames configuration and operation outcomes together. Legacy encrypted servers-only files remain readable, and ordinary saves retain that format while no operation journal exists. The first recorded configuration operation upgrades to a v2 envelope; later formal edits preserve its receipts. Older binaries cannot read v2. There is no automatic journal eviction/downgrade: 10,000 recorded operations is an explicit capacity boundary. Post-commit metadata publication can be reconciled without discovery or rewriting the saved configuration. This assumes one platform authority manager; shared-data multi-process authority writes are not certified.

775.author: ink999107
775.body:
#699 was argued with measurements: the catalog row had grown to 106 MB and every
save rewrote it, and after the side-table split the row is about 0.4 MB and a
save costs milliseconds. The tests that came with it guarded the shape of that
change — nothing stays inline, a repeat snapshot republishes nothing, a delete
answers before it reclaims — but not the numbers. Provenance could drift back
into the catalog row and the suite would stay green.

## Two guards, on the shape rather than a clock reading

`services/api/src/store-performance.test.ts` creates a Project and a Session,
records 3,000 revisions through the public store API, and then reads the
database the way an operator would:

- the catalog row grows by less than 256 B, stays under 64 KiB, and does not
  contain the recorded paths;
- `workspace_files` and `workspace_file_revisions` hold 3,000 rows each, and the
  bytes they carry are more than ten times the catalog row;
- the last recorded path is read back out of a side row, so rows that exist but
  say nothing cannot pass the count.

Against the pre-split store the same fixture adds 2,139,778 B to the row, so the
first commit that puts the collections back fails with a number in the message
rather than with a mystery.

The second test compares the median of one catalog save — a mutation that
changes a single string — on an empty catalog and on one with those 3,000
revisions. This is a ratio, not a millisecond budget: the bound is 10x the empty
median and never below 10 ms. Measured here, 0.492 ms before and 0.383 ms after;
the pre-split store takes 27.675 ms on the same fixture, about 56x, and cannot
pass. A slow or busy machine inflates both medians together.

## The three waits a user feels, with a budget in seconds

The shape guards say the write path is right; they do not say the product is
fast. These are the numbers a user actually felt on the live catalog behind
#699 — 71,000 provenance records, 39 subagents — measured with #699's store,
artifact-listing, deletion and CAS files reverted in a scratch worktree:

| Flow | Scale | Before #699 | After #699 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Switch to a Session | 70,000 provenance rows, 500 workspace files | **4.7 s** | **2.0 s** on the first visit (1.7–4.1 s across runs), **0.24 s** once warm |
| Delete a Session | 2,000 messages, 3,000 workspace files | **8.1 s** | **70 ms** |
| Delete its Project | ten such Sessions | **14.4 s** | **304 ms** |

The deletions are the requests a user describes as a hang: the request used to
reclaim the Session's data before answering, and now answers when the catalog
commits and reclaims behind it. The switch is the case the split did not make
instant — the first visit after a workspace change still reconciles against the
provenance index, and the desktop's replay rebuild and transcript render sit on
top of that. The settings lists were not a regression (17 ms before, 16 ms
after on the heavy fixture); their test exists so that an endpoint cannot start
doing catalog-wide work unnoticed.

What `services/api/src/performance-budget.test.ts` asserts is the same four
flows on a fixture that runs in about eight seconds, with budgets loose enough
for a shared CI machine:

| Flow | Fixture in the test | Budget | After #699 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Switch to a Session | 800 messages, 200 runs, 500 files | 1 s | 75 ms |
| Settings page | empty Project | 0.5 s | 16 ms |
| Delete a Session | 800 messages, 200 runs, 500 files | 1 s | 49 ms |
| Delete a Project | 6 Sessions × (200 messages, 20 runs, 100 files) | 1.5 s | 114 ms |

Against the pre-#699 store on this fixture the two deletion cases fail with
1,822 ms and 1,999 ms — above their 1 s and 1.5 s budgets — so those guards
would have caught the regression. Switching and the settings lists measure tens
of milliseconds either way at this size, so their budgets are guards against
future work proportional to the catalog rather than evidence of a past win; the
ratio guard above and the live-scale numbers are what pin that marginal cost.
The budgets are deliberately loose — 13x to 30x the observed cost — because a
wall clock belongs to the machine, and a fourteen-second guard would never fail.

### What this test does not cover, and why the small fixture is not the whole story

The budget fixture holds 500 workspace files. The catalog behind #699 held
71,000 records and 73,000 revisions, and at that size the same switch is a
different number: measured on a 70,000-row catalog, the three requests took
**4.7 s** before the change and **2.0 s** on the first visit after a workspace
change (1.7–4.1 s across runs; the listing reconciles against the 70k-row
index), then **236 ms** once that listing is warm; the Session and runs reads
alone are 38 ms and 45 ms. A desktop switch also rebuilds every finished run from its own
event log, one request per run, which an HTTP test of three metadata routes
does not include: 100 runs × 300 events (12 MB) fetched and folded in 0.73 s,
200 runs × 1,000 events (83 MB) in 2.8 s on this host. That rebuild, plus a
slower disk and the transcript render, is what turns seconds into the tens of
seconds a long session used to take. The budgets here guard the metadata
route; they are not a promise about the whole switch until the replay rebuild
has a budget of its own.

Each test asserts the payload is the work, not an empty answer: the switch
carries 800 messages, 200 runs and 500 files, the settings lists are non-empty,
and a deletion is followed by a `404`. What the budgets catch is an endpoint
that starts doing work proportional to the whole catalog, where the cost is
seconds; the ratio guards above are what pin the marginal cost.

The first request into a freshly started API pays about 230 ms of module loading
on this host, whichever endpoint it is. That belongs to start-up, not to a
switch, so each fixture warms up on an empty Session before the stopwatch
starts.

## The probe budget is a number too

`services/api/src/remote-compute.test.ts` gains a machine that accepts the
connection and never answers. The settings page reads `checking` without
waiting, a burst of renders joins the single ask already in flight, and the
probe is abandoned at its 8 s budget with the message naming it. The next
render then reads that bounded answer instead of starting the wait again. The
test drives the budget with mock timers, so it does not spend 8 s of CI time.
`REACHABILITY_TIMEOUT_MS` is exported from `@sciencediscovery/executor` so the
test ticks the constant the client actually waits on: changing the budget moves
the test with it instead of leaving a second copy of the number behind.

## Validation

- `node --import tsx --test src/store-performance.test.ts src/remote-compute.test.ts src/store.test.ts src/performance-budget.test.ts`
  in `services/api`: 151 tests, 151 passed, 0 failed. The budget suite was run
  three more times on its own, 4/4 each time.
- Every budget is the median of three sequential samples: the UT layer runs
  four workers on one machine, and a single GC pause must not decide a budget.
  The deletion cases seed three identical Sessions or Projects, because a
  delete cannot be repeated on the same target. The warm-up now also hits the
  five endpoints the settings budget measures, so that case passes when run on
  its own (`--test-name-pattern`) instead of inheriting a warm process from the
  case before it.
- The two shape guards run against the pre-split `store.ts` (the module extracted
  from the commit before #699) fail with the numbers quoted above.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` and
  `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable: no behaviour changes. The only production edit is exporting
`REACHABILITY_TIMEOUT_MS`, a constant that already existed; every suite
exercises the existing store, API and RemoteComputeClient code paths.

## Release

Release category: release:internal (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer:
this account has no write access to the upstream repository)
User impact: none directly; the tests keep the catalog write path and the three
most common waits from silently regressing.
Compatibility and migration: none.


Part of #800 (new UI performance optimization).

778.body:
Fixes #777

Owner: Dev2
Written-by: Dev-2
Tip SHA: 0bb3ee16884843a09d30278a63db007ba3f4da5d
Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c (main at push; branch rebased onto it, no overlap)

`web_fetch`/`web_search` handed search-result titles and snippets to the model with named HTML references still encoded. Only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp` decoded, so a page title like `Café — a review` reached the prompt and the report verbatim, and the sources a science search cites most often (encyclopedias, European sites) are exactly the entity-heavy ones. This decodes every named reference a browser resolves, in the same single pass as before.

## What changed

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts`: the five-name map is replaced by the full WHATWG named character reference set — 2125 semicolon-terminated names — expanded into a `Map` once at module load. `nbsp` keeps its existing ordinary-space mapping; numeric references, the single-pass rule (`&lt;` → `<`) and unknown names (`&bogus;` stays literal) are unchanged. The decoding loop is the same one-scan replace it was; only the data changed shape and moved out of this module.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html-entities.ts` (new): the table itself — a `name;code point;…` constant, 246 folded lines — under a 37-line header that states the source (WHATWG named character references via CPython's `html.entities.html5`, 2231 keys of which the 2125 semicolon forms are what this pattern accepts), the retrieval date, the exact `python3` snippet that regenerates the body, and the licence position: the standard's table reproduced as factual data — names and code points any HTML parser needs — not copied from another project's source. `html.ts` keeps the decoder and goes from 79 lines to 90 (+11); 368 is only the shape this branch's previous commit had with the table inline, and this commit moves it out. The data is 246 of the new file's 284 lines.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: one line, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. The import in `html.ts` keeps a `.ts` extension so `node --experimental-strip-types` — the command the issue reproduces with — resolves the sibling source instead of failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; that option is what lets tsc accept the specifier and still emit `./html-entities.js` (verified: the built `dist/web/native/html.js` line is `import { NAMED_ENTITIES_PACKED } from "./html-entities.js";`). It belongs in the base config rather than the package one: the root tests config used by `pnpm typecheck` extends only `tsconfig.base.json`, and with the option in `packages/data-source/tsconfig.json` alone that check fails with `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts(73,39): error TS5097: An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled.` From the base config both the package build and that check pass. It changes nothing else in the tree — the only `test/` file that `tsc` type-checks imports `.js` paths; the Playwright specs under `test/` are not in any tsconfig.
- `html-entities.ts` is force-added: `.gitignore`'s `data-*/` rule also matches the `packages/data-source/` directory (`git check-ignore -v` reports `.gitignore:91`). I left that rule alone to keep this PR single-purpose; say the word if you would rather have it anchored as `/data-*/` and I will open a separate issue.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts`: cases for the names in the issue (`eacute`, `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `apos`, `diams`, `rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, Latin-1, symbols), case sensitivity, an unknown name, the single-pass rule after the table widened, and a guard that the exported table still has exactly 2125 entries plus one two-scalar value (`NotEqualTilde`), so a dropped or mis-chunked line cannot pass as a smaller table. The test file is unchanged by the move.

Size, whole PR: 4 files, 344 insertions, 8 deletions (`html-entities.ts` +284, `html.test.ts` +41/−1, `html.ts` +18/−7, `tsconfig.base.json` +1).

## Red first

Decoder tests. Command:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/html.test.ts
```

Before the fix:

```
# Subtest: decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
not ok 3 - decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
  expected: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
  actual: 'café — 5–10 … O'Brien'
# Subtest: decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
not ok 4 - decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
  expected: 'Ää'
  actual: 'Ää'
# pass 5
# fail 2
```

Table guard. The guard lands in its own commit before the export exists, so it is red on the change that adds only the test:

```
# pass 0
# fail 1
SyntaxError: The requested module './html.js' does not provide an export named 'NAMED_ENTITIES'
```

and it fails the way it is meant to when one entry is dropped from the packed constant (mutation check, one `AElig;c6;` field removed, then restored):

```
not ok 8 - keeps every entry of the generated WHATWG table
  expected: 2125
  actual: 2124
# pass 7
# fail 1
```

Green after the implementation, same command as the decoder run: `# pass 8`, `# fail 0`. The package suite goes from 74 to 75 tests with the guard: `# tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0`.

## The issue's reproduction

Command from #777:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

On this tip:

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

The middle line is the single-pass guarantee: the decoded ampersand does not start a second scan.

## Gates

On this tip, in `packages/data-source` unless noted:

```
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json                                        # exit 0 (build)

## Base

## Red first

The test commit alone, on `main` `2f22d16f`:

```
$ cd apps/desktop && node --import tsx --test tests/xlsx.test.ts
not ok 11 - a shared string's phonetic run is not part of the cell
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
    +   '漢字カンジ',
    -   '漢字',
        '山川'
      ]
not ok 12 - an inline string's phonetic run is not part of the cell
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
    +   '東京トウキョウ',
    -   '東京'
      ]
not ok 13 - rich text runs keep their text and drop the phonetic run
# tests 13
# pass 10
# fail 3
```

`actual: '漢字カンジ'` against `expected: '漢字'`, and `actual: '東京トウキョウ'` against `expected: '東京'`: the reading inside `<rPh>` was read as if it were cell text.

## Why it happened

`apps/desktop/src/app/xlsx.ts:66-71` collected the text of every `<t>` under the string element. The spreadsheet grammar for a string is `CT_Rst = (t | r | rPh)*`, and `<rPh>` is the phonetic guide Excel draws above the cell — it is not part of the value. Both `readSharedStrings` (each `<si>`) and the `inlineStr` branch of `cellText` (each `<is>`) went through that collector, so every guided cell was read twice.

## What changed

`textRuns` now drops the `<rPh>` subtree before it scans for `<t>` runs:

```ts
const withoutPhonetics = xml.replace(/<rPh\b[^>]*\/>|<rPh\b[^>]*>[\s\S]*?<\/rPh>/gu, "");
```

- Both forms in written workbooks are covered: the paired `<rPh …>…</rPh>` and the self-closing `<rPh …/>`.
- The runs are still collected the same way afterwards, so `<t>` content and entity decoding are untouched.
- Rich text (`<r><t>東</t></r><r><t>京</t></r>`) still reads as `東京`, with or without an `<rPh>` sibling.
- `date1904`, number formats, shared-string indexing and sheet order are not touched; only the string element's text runs changed.

- Ran: `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit` → exit 0.
- Not run here: `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — a local `pnpm check` step, not a GitHub Actions step (CI runs `ci:l1`, `ci:ut`, `ci:st` and `ci:e2e`) — reports 7 module-resolution errors in this checkout (`packages/execution-router`: `Cannot find module '@sciencediscovery/schema'` / `'@sciencediscovery/sandbox-capability'`; `services/api`: `Cannot find module '@sciencediscovery/execution-router'` and two implicit `any`s) because the new `packages/execution-router` has no `node_modules` here and `pnpm install` cannot repair it (the pnpm store is read-only). Those errors belong to this checkout: the same command exits 0 on a clean install of an earlier `main` checkout (`8bcc2237`, 2026-11-01). The tsconfig's include list does not cover `apps/desktop/tests`, so it would not typecheck this PR's test file anyway.
- Not run: no browser or DOM interaction — the reader is DOM-free and its tests build workbooks in memory with `fflate`; there is no rendered surface to inspect.

When an error escapes a streaming route after headers have been committed, the outer HTTP handler attempts a second response and rejects with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT. Related to #779. The production exception that initially interrupted the stream remains unidentified; this change prevents the secondary headers-sent failure and preserves diagnostics. Keep the issue open for production confirmation.

The guard belongs at the common request catch rather than only its unclassified branch: classified errors such as ENOENT have the same failure mode. Keeping send()/sendError() unchanged preserves normal response contracts and lets the request catch log the original exception with request context.

Hosted UT/ST/E2E must finish before merge.

Release category: release:fix

The completed run 41581903193 reported 6101 UT identities: 6100 passed and one failed, `cancelling a recovery probe releases both its slot and the single probe permit` in source-health.test.ts. The SSE regression passed; ST and all five mocked E2E shards passed as well.

fix(api): charge the cached prompt span once in usage cost estimates

Fixes #783

Owner: Dev2
Written-by: Dev-2
Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c (main)
Tip SHA: 4b6b9d184b024e32813055d5da502cb9609aa831

A Chat Completions call reports `prompt_tokens` with the cache hits already inside it, and DeepSeek additionally reports the uncached remainder as `prompt_cache_miss_tokens`. The Usage page estimate charged `inputTokens` at the full input rate, added `cacheReadTokens` again at the cached rate, and then charged the miss count as a cache write. For 1,000,000 prompt tokens of which 800,000 were cache hits it estimated **2.804 CNY** where the provider charges **0.804** — 3.49x — and **4.004** against **2.004** when no cached rate is published. The same numbers on an Anthropic Messages record estimate 2.404 correctly, because there `input_tokens` excludes `cache_read_input_tokens`; that asymmetry is what locates the defect at the dialect boundary rather than in the pricing table.

## What changed

- `services/api/src/model-usage.ts`: `estimateInvocationCost` now takes the dialect that produced the record. For the OpenAI-shaped dialects (`openai-chat-completions` and `openai-responses`, whose prompt/input count already contains the cached span) it charges `inputTokens - cacheReadTokens` at the input rate and the hits at `cachedInput` — or at the input rate when no cached rate is published — so the same span is never charged twice. Chat Completions additionally has no cache-write charge: its recorded write count is `prompt_cache_miss_tokens`, the uncached prompt that the first term already covers, so it is not charged a second time. Anthropic Messages keeps its own arithmetic, write charge included.
- `ModelUsageAnalyticsContext` gains `protocolByModelProfileId`, and `summarizeModelUsageAnalytics` passes each record's profile dialect into the estimate.
- `services/api/src/store.ts` builds that map from the model catalog, resolving a profile the way the model client does: its `apiProtocol`, else an `/api/plan` endpoint means `anthropic-messages`, else `openai-chat-completions`.
- Why the dialect is resolved at pricing time instead of changing `normalizeUsage`: the recorded counts are also what the product reports back on the wire (the JiuwenSwarm gateway emits `prompt_tokens` together with `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, and `packages/model/src/completion.ts` echoes the same shape), and they are what the Usage page shows as input and cache-read tokens. The estimate, by contrast, is computed at render time from stored counts — so this fixes new records and also corrects the figure shown for history. That means past chat estimates drop on the Usage page, which is the intended outcome. Records whose model profile no longer exists have no dialect to resolve and keep the previous arithmetic.
- `services/api/src/model-usage.test.ts`: USG-018 feeds the issue's payload through `normalizeUsage(..., "openai-chat-completions")` and pins 0.804 and 2.004 beside an Anthropic control at 2.404; USG-019 runs both through the analytics summary with per-profile dialects and covers the profile-to-dialect resolution the store uses. The existing USG-015 6.65 assertion is untouched and still passes.
- The issue's acceptance text says 2.0008 for the no-cached-rate case; the arithmetic is 500 × 8 / 1e6 = 0.004 on top of 2.000, i.e. **2.004**, which is also what the issue's own probe prints. The test pins 2.004.

Size, whole PR: 3 files, 160 insertions, 5 deletions (`model-usage.test.ts` +115, `model-usage.ts` +35/−4, `store.ts` +10/−1).

## Validation

Red first: USG-018 and USG-019 land before the fix and fail on it with `2.804 !== 0.804` (the estimate the issue reports), then pass with it.

Ran on this branch's tip, rebased onto `a429ba1d` (no overlap with anything upstream merged since):

- Issue probe before the fix: `normalizeUsage` → input 1,000,000 / cacheRead 800,000 / cacheWrite 200,000; `estimateInvocationCost` → 2.804 with `cachedInput: 0.5`, 4.004 without it; Anthropic shape 2.404.
- Issue probe after the fix: chat with the dialect → **0.804** and **2.004**; Anthropic shape → **2.404**, unchanged; the legacy two-argument call still prints 2.804, which is the documented no-dialect behaviour.
- `cd packages/model && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` → 136 tests, 136 pass, 0 fail.
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` → 1774 tests, 1769 pass, 5 fail, 0 cancelled. All five are host prerequisites, not assertions: four need Python modules missing from this checkout (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'reportlab'` ×3, `No module named 'uvicorn'` ×1), and one needs the optional `@openai/codex-linux-x64` binary package (`Cannot find module '@openai/codex-linux-x64/package.json'`).
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/model-usage.test.ts` → 12 tests, 12 pass.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` (services/api) → exit 0.
- `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → exit 0, all packages done.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` (the root tests config used by `pnpm typecheck`) → exit 0.
- `pnpm ci:l1` → PASS, **4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed / 0 failed**.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` → `Architecture boundaries OK (332 package source files checked)`.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut` / `pnpm ci:st` / `pnpm ci:e2e`: blocked at their prepare step on this host — `uv sync --project services/paper --locked` fails with `Read-only file system (os error 30) at path /home/xuke/.cache/uv/.tmp...`, so those layers never reach the tests. The UT tests they would run are the direct per-package runs reported above.
- Docker and Binary gates: not applicable to this change and not run.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED for a first-class journey: the only user-visible effect is the estimated cost number on the Usage page, no mocked browser journey reads that page, and a stack-level check would need a recorded Chat Completions invocation with cache hits. The arithmetic is covered by the analytics unit tests above instead.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the category this change belongs in; our token cannot write labels on the upstream repository — adding labels there requires admin rights (403) — so a maintainer needs to apply it).
User impact: the estimated cost for Chat Completions models on the Usage page drops to the provider's actual billing shape — the 3.49x overestimate is gone, including for already-recorded invocations. Token counts shown are unchanged.
Compatibility and migration: none; no stored data, API shape or wire format changes.

fix(artifact-manager): treat a missing content-length as unknown

Fixes #788

Owner: Dev2
Written-by: Dev-2
Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c (main)
Tip SHA: 37bc58c01c0473ed32d7d13c486046bda823f77e

A governed download whose response is chunked (no `content-length`) recorded `totalBytes: 0` and reported 100% while the body was still arriving. `parseTotalBytes` did `Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))`, and `Headers.get()` returns `null` for an absent header while `Number(null)` is `0`, so "unknown" became "zero bytes": `totalBytes` 0 flowed into `updateProgress`, whose `totalBytes ? … : 100` branch stored `percent: 100`, and the completed job kept `totalBytes: 0`. This is the normal path for the in-repo MCP sources, which emit no `expectedBytes`, so `parseTotalBytes` is the only size signal such a download has; `totalBytes = 0` also skipped the pre-flight quota check.

## What changed

- `packages/artifact-manager/src/governed-download-manager.ts`: `parseTotalBytes` reads the header explicitly and treats `null` as unknown (`Number.NaN`) instead of zero. ## E2E user journeys

The card's own rendering line (`job.progress.percent ?? 0`) is not changed here — with `percent` absent it now prints 0% instead of a false 100% while bytes still arrive. That file is `apps/web`, outside this issue's file list; the card rendering is tracked separately in #792.

793.author: HugoXK
793.body:
Fixes #792

## What

`apps/web/src/GovernedDownloadCards.tsx` printed `{job.progress.percent ?? 0}%`, so a chunked download — no `content-length`, hence no `totalBytes` and, once #791 lands, no `percent` at all — showed `0%` for its whole life, including after it reached `completed`, while the byte count beside it climbed. "Unknown size" read as "not started".

The line is now one helper, `progressLine`: state · percentage (only when `percent` is present) · bytes moved. A job without `percent` prints `running · 1,048,576 bytes`; a job with `percent: 42` still prints `42%`.

796.author: ink999107
796.body:
The Settings dialog unmounts a pane whenever the user selects another group, so
every visit to 技能 / MCP 服务器 / 专家 started from an empty `useLoaded`, drew
the dashed `正在读取…` frame, and only then painted the list. The answer arrives
in tens of milliseconds, but the frame is what a user remembers: the pane looks
like it reloads from scratch every time, which is what makes it feel slower than
the other agent platforms whose settings open instantly. The web app already
keeps a pane's last answer beside its client
(`apps/web/src/settings-cache.ts`); the desktop app had no such store.

## What changed

- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings-cache.ts` — the same
  `WeakMap<client, Map<key, value>>` shape as the web copy, deliberately with the
  same names and the same contract: only answers that are cheap to show stale
  (a list, a status, a flag) are kept there.
- `useLoaded(load, remember?)` — with `remember`, the hook seeds its state from
  the cache on mount (and again if the key changes while the page stays
  mounted), paints that value, and refreshes behind it; a successful read is
  written back. Without `remember`, every existing page behaves exactly as
  before, including the loading gate on first paint.
- The three list panes opt in, keyed `skills:<projectId>`, `mcp-servers` and
  `specialists`. The Project is part of the Skills key because the enabled set
  is project-scoped: switching Projects must never paint the previous one's
  switches.
- Pages whose first paint is a form the user is about to edit (timeouts, the
  sandbox network policy, runtime defaults) keep the loading gate. A cached
  value there could be edited before the refresh lands, and the write would be
  computed from a value the server has already moved past.

A remembered value is a starting point, not an answer: the read starts
immediately and its result replaces what is on screen. If that read fails, the
failure is drawn above the list instead of replacing it, with the retry the
error section already had — the remembered answer is exactly what a user wants
to keep looking at while the service is unreachable, and dropping it would undo
the first paint this change is about. A pane with no answer to keep still shows
the failure alone. The window in which a user could act on a remembered list is
one round trip — the settings endpoints measure at about 16 ms on the fixture in
#699's budget test.

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`: 689 passed, 0 failed,
  0 skipped (492 subtests across 95 suites), including five new render tests
  in `apps/desktop/tests/settings-cache.test.tsx`: a remembered list paints
  without the loading frame, one client's list never paints under another, one
  Project's enabled Skills never paint as another's, a failed refresh keeps the
  list it painted and draws the failure above it, and a pane with no answer to
  keep shows the failure alone.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts` gains two Playwright cases.
  One holds the `/api/skills` response, switches 技能 → 专家 → 技能, and asserts
  the list is on screen while the refresh is still in flight; it passes with
  this change and fails without it. The other makes every later read of the
  list return 503 and asserts the remembered list stays visible under the
  retry; it also passes with this change and fails without it. Both pin the
  behaviour rather than the timing. The full spec is 23 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`: clean.
- `node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs run --slice ut` on `96c49856` (the
  previous head; the diff since then is `apps/desktop` only):
  535 groups, 6,068 planned / 6,068 executed / 6,065 passed / 0 skipped /
  3 failed, no provider faults. The three failures are outside this diff, which
  touches only `apps/desktop`:
  - `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` — `bwrap: Unknown option
    --disable-userns`: the host's bubblewrap is older than the test expects.
  - `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` — passes when re-run alone (6.7 s); it
    failed only inside the parallel slice.
  - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` (the trajectory
    case) — reproduces alone; `services/api` is byte-identical to the base
    commit, and the case does not import anything from `apps/desktop`.
  The slice's own teardown then hung on this host (the swarm hold process
  never exited), so the counts above are aggregated from the 535 per-group
  `summary.json` files rather than the runner's top-level summary.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — desktop browser (Playwright, mocked control plane), SHA under test is
the head of this branch.

- 设置 › 技能, switch to 专家 and back: the remembered skill list is drawn
  before the refresh answers, and `正在读取…` is not drawn. Covered by
  `switching back paints the remembered list before the refresh answers`.
- 设置 › 技能, switch away and back while every `/api/skills` read fails: the
  remembered list stays on screen under a 重试 button instead of being
  replaced by the error section. Covered by `a refresh that fails keeps the
  remembered list under the failure`.
- Existing desktop settings journeys in the same spec (skill switch writes,
  MCP server edit and delete, specialist edit, the model provider chain) still
  pass against the same pane code.

Not covered: the real local stack with the Python control plane — no journey in
`.e2e` opens the desktop settings dialog, so the mocked browser suite is the
level this change is exercised at.

## Release

Release category: release:fix (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer: this
account has no write access to the upstream repository)
User impact: opening 技能, MCP 服务器 or 专家 in Settings now shows the last list
immediately instead of flashing a loading frame on every visit.
Compatibility and migration: none.


Part of #800 (new UI performance optimization).
